assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling turned aryl amine construction from a harsh, narrow problem into a routine operation. It is among the most used reactions in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis, and ligand design (bulky phosphines, later biaryl phosphines) made it general. This is the kind of general bond-forming method I weigh most heavily; the adoption is visible in countless syntheses and process routes.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the catalytic, ligand-controlled, broadly applicable amination in the mid-1990s onward. Kosugi (and Migita) reported earlier aminostannane couplings that are precursors but not the general method; I am not certain how a committee would weigh that priority. Two laureates is a clean configuration.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of independent confirmation, industrial use at scale, and stable mechanistic understanding. The 2010 Pd cross-coupling prize covered C-C coupling, so this is a distinct but adjacent contribution; recognition is mature and timely.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2010 Nobel Prize for Pd-catalyzed cross-coupling may be judged too close.
Role of Kosugi and Migita as precursors is uncertain from the supplied text and my memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis opened radical and single-electron pathways under mild conditions, enabling new disconnections and late-stage functionalization, and is now widely used in medicinal and process chemistry. Chemically new, conceptually simple (a photocatalyst as a redox shuttle), and broadly adopted.
assessment.attribution: MacMillan, Yoon and Stephenson published the foundational synthetic photoredox papers in 2008-2009. Konig, Fukuzumi, Nicewicz and Melchiorre also made major contributions, and credit for the earliest steps is contested. MacMillan already shared the 2021 prize for organocatalysis, which may weigh against him; I would accept alternatives among the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Field is more than fifteen years old with extensive independent validation and industrial uptake, though some scaling and reproducibility issues remain. Timing is good.
uncertainties: Contested priority among six or seven contributors.
MacMillan's 2021 prize may reduce his candidacy, and the three-person limit forces a hard cut.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Selective C-H functionalization lets chemists treat C-H bonds as functional groups, shortening syntheses, which is the efficiency theme at the core of my field. Directing-group, ligand and template control has made remote and site-selective C-H transformations practical in natural product and drug synthesis.
assessment.attribution: Yu is the leading figure for ligand-enabled Pd C-H activation and templates, Sanford for Pd/oxidant catalysis and mechanism, Hartwig for Ir-catalyzed borylation. Daugulis and Smith also contributed, and the field is broad enough that a fair three-person split is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Substantial independent confirmation and growing industrial use, but practicality at scale is still uneven compared with cross-coupling. Reasonably mature, perhaps slightly early.
uncertainties: Breadth of the field complicates attribution.
Industrial adoption is less universal than for cross-coupling.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation reframes small-molecule pharmacology: induced proximity to E3 ligases removes a target rather than inhibiting it. The chemistry of heterobifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues (including the thalidomide mechanism) is original and drug candidates are in late-stage clinical trials. I would ask what is new chemically; the answer is the design principle and ligand chemistry for E3 recruitment.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated PROTACs; Ciulli contributed VHL ligands and structural rationale. Handa, Ito and others established the cereblon/IMiD glue mechanism, which is a separate strand. Eight credited names make a clean prize hard; the PROTAC and glue streams may need separate recognition.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is still emerging, with no approved PROTAC degrader yet to my knowledge, so recognition may be premature, though the concept is well reproduced.
uncertainties: Clinical outcomes are not yet proven.
Allocation between PROTAC and molecular-glue discoverers is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation made chemical total synthesis and semisynthesis of proteins routine, joining unprotected peptides chemoselectively. It is a general, conceptually simple method that changed access to proteins for study, including modified proteins and D-protein work.
assessment.attribution: Kent and Dawson reported NCL in 1994, and Muir extended it with expressed protein ligation; Danishefsky, Brik and Liu applied and extended it. Kent, Dawson and Muir appear the most defensible trio, though Muir's contribution is a semisynthetic extension.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of use, stable and well confirmed. Timely, though some may feel its biology-facing applications overshadow the chemistry.
uncertainties: Whether Muir's expressed protein ligation merits co-recognition versus Danishefsky is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Isolation of stable carbenes (imidazol-2-ylidenes and persistent carbenes) created a new class of ligands and organocatalysts, underpinning modern Ru metathesis catalysts and Pd and Au catalysis. The impact on synthesis is wide, and the discovery was conceptually surprising.
assessment.attribution: Arduengo isolated the first crystalline NHC in 1991, Bertrand the first stable carbenes (phosphinocarbene, 1988, and later CAAC), Nolan developed NHC-metal catalysts. Bode and Rovis are organocatalysis contributors and are less central to the core discovery.
assessment.maturity: Mature with long and broad confirmation; recognition is arguably overdue and fits the catalysis tradition already honored by the 2005 and 2010 prizes.
uncertainties: Bertrand's priority claim on earlier carbenes versus Arduengo is a historical dispute I cannot settle.
Nolan's role is more developmental than foundational.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Phosphoramidite chemistry made automated, high-fidelity oligonucleotide synthesis possible and underlies PCR primers, sequencing, gene synthesis and nucleic acid therapeutics. It is a very practical method with enormous adoption.
assessment.attribution: Caruthers developed the phosphoramidite method in the early 1980s; Hood is credited mainly for instrument automation, so a single laureate looks most defensible. Others such as Letsinger (phosphite triester) are not on the supplied list and I cannot weigh them here.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and universally confirmed; recognition is very late and some may judge it as technology rather than discovery.
uncertainties: Whether the prize committee views this as methodology versus enabling technology.
Credit relative to precursors outside the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom transfer radical polymerization gave controlled radical polymerization with defined architecture and low dispersity under practical conditions, widely used in materials design. It is general and chemically clear, though the field is more polymer-oriented than my own.
assessment.attribution: Matyjaszewski and Sawamoto reported the Cu and Ru ATRP systems independently in 1995; Wang worked with Matyjaszewski and Kamigaito with Sawamoto. A Matyjaszewski-Sawamoto pair is the cleanest split, and I list a third name only as an option.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed, with substantial industrial use. RAFT (a separate candidate) is a competing controlled-radical contribution, so any prize may need to address both.
uncertainties: Competition and possible joint recognition with RAFT.
